34 A battery is marked 9.0 V.
What does this mean?
A
Each coulomb of charge from the battery supplies 9.0 J of electrical energy to the whole
circuit.
B
The battery supplies 9.0 J of electrical energy to an external circuit for each coulomb of
charge.
C
The potential difference across any component connected to the battery will be 9.0 V.
D
There will always be a potential difference of 9.0 V across the battery terminals.

hints: Notice the question asks what the printed 9.0 V on the battery itself means, not the voltage measured across one component in a circuit.
Connect voltage to energy per charge using $E = W/Q$, where $E$ is e.m.f. in volts, $W$ is electrical energy in joules and $Q$ is charge in coulombs.
Compare energy given to the whole circuit with energy given only to the external circuit, and ask whether terminal p.d. must always stay at 9.0 V when current flows.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: the battery is labelled $9.0 \text{ V}$. This label states its electromotive force (e.m.f.), the characteristic of the source on open circuit.
State the governing definition: e.m.f. is electrical energy supplied by the source per unit charge, $E = W/Q$, measured in $\text{J C}^{-1}$ which is the volt.
Substitute the values: for $E = 9.0 \text{ V}$ and $Q = 1 \text{ C}$, $W = E Q = 9.0 \times 1 = 9.0 \text{ J}$. So each coulomb receives $9.0 \text{ J}$ from the battery.
Explain the whole-circuit point: that $9.0 \text{ J}$ per coulomb drives charge around the complete loop, including work done against internal resistance and in the external circuit.

Rule out the alternatives: energy to the external circuit alone is terminal p.d., not e.m.f.; a single component need not get the full $9.0 \text{ V}$; terminal p.d. drops below $9.0 \text{ V}$ when current flows.
Therefore each coulomb from the battery supplies $9.0 \text{ J}$ to the whole circuit. This is option A.

A.explanation: Correct. The 9.0 V mark is the e.m.f., so each $1 \text{ C}$ moved by the battery is given $9.0 \text{ J}$ of electrical energy for the whole circuit including internal resistance.

B.explanation: Incorrect. Energy delivered only to the external circuit per coulomb is the terminal p.d., which is less than $9.0 \text{ V}$ when current flows through internal resistance.

C.explanation: Incorrect. In a circuit with more than one component the $9.0 \text{ V}$ is shared, so an individual component has less than $9.0 \text{ V}$ across it.

D.explanation: Incorrect. Terminal p.d. equals e.m.f. only on open circuit and falls below $9.0 \text{ V}$ when current causes lost volts inside the battery.
